__Back end structuring and data storage__

__Proposed Backend Structure:__

__	•	Core Services Layer \(Unified\):__ This is the heart of your backend\. It's agnostic to whether the request comes from the Web App or the PPT Add\-in\. It handles all the heavy lifting related to the Project Knowledge Base\.

__	•	ProjectManagementService:__

	•	Manages project creation, updates, user associations\.

	•	Handles user authentication and authorization for project access\.

__	•	DocumentIngestionService \(Asynchronous Pipeline \- as per your PKB spec\):__

	•	Receives uploaded files\.

	•	Orchestrates parsing, chunking\.

	•	Manages interaction with embedding models\.

	•	Stores processed data \(chunks, embeddings, metadata\) in the database\(s\)\.

	•	Orchestrates AI\-driven Document Content Type assignment and initial Document Purpose generation\.

	•	Triggers the SummarizationMetadataService\.

__	•	SummarizationMetadataService:__

	•	Takes processed document content/chunks and user\-provided context \(Document Role/Purpose Category, userNoteOnPurpose, validated Document Content Type\)\.

	•	Constructs and sends prompts to the LLM \(using your Group A, B, C, D logic\)\.

	•	Parses LLM responses and stores the structured summaries and extracted metadata\.

__	•	QueryService / RAGService \(for "Ask Project Docs"\):__

	•	Receives user queries and project context\.

	•	Performs vector search \(with metadata filtering for project isolation and Document Role/Purpose Category / Document Content Type focus, if applicable\)\.

	•	Handles re\-ranking \(if implemented\)\.

	•	Assembles context for the LLM\.

	•	Constructs and sends Q&A prompts to the LLM\.

	•	Processes LLM responses, including citation handling\.

__	•	ConsultingCraftService \(Future, but good to conceptualize\):__

	•	Provides access to generic and \(later\) enterprise\-specific consulting best practices, frameworks, and stylistic guidance\. Could be used by other services to refine LLM prompts or evaluate outputs\.

__	•	AnalyticsService \(Future\):__ Logs anonymized usage patterns for product improvement\.

__	•	API Gateway / Main API Layer \(Unified Entry Point\):__

	•	A single entry point for all client requests \(Web App, PPT Add\-in\)\.

	•	Handles initial request validation, authentication, rate limiting\.

	•	Routes requests to the appropriate API Facade/Adapter or directly to Core Services if the interface is simple enough\.

__	•	API Facades / Adapters \(Client\-Specific Logic\):__

__	•	WebAppAPIFacade:__

	•	Exposes endpoints specifically tailored for the Web App's needs\.

	•	Might handle slightly different data transformation or aggregation logic compared to the Add\-in\.

	•	For "Ask Project Docs," it would provide the full\-featured interface\.

	•	Handles requests for dashboard data, full summary views, at\-a\-glance insights, etc\.

__	•	PPTAddInAPIFacade:__

	•	Exposes endpoints optimized for the PowerPoint Add\-in\.

	•	For "Ask Project Docs \(Lite\)," this facade might implement logic to simplify the query or the response format for the more constrained add\-in UI\.

	•	Handles requests for title generation, bullet drafting, outline structuring, based on *current slide context* passed from the add\-in, plus project context\. It will call the Core Services, possibly with slightly different prompting nuances or data packaging\.

	•	This is where you manage the "lite" version logic\.

__Why this Unified Core \+ Facades Approach?__

__	•	Code Reusability:__ Core logic for document processing, RAG, summarization, database interaction is written once\.

__	•	Consistency:__ Ensures both clients operate on the same data and business rules\.

__	•	Maintainability:__ Easier to update core logic; changes benefit both clients\.

__	•	Scalability:__ Core services can be scaled independently\.

__	•	Flexibility:__ Facades allow you to tailor the API for each client without altering the core\. If you add a mobile app later, you just add a MobileAPIFacade\.

__	•	Clear Separation of Concerns:__ Core services focus on business logic; facades focus on client\-specific API contracts\.

__	•	Ease of Understanding for Future Coders:__ This layered architecture is a standard and well\-understood pattern\.

__II\. Database Structure & Management__

__Core Principle: Shared, Unified Database\(s\) for the Project Knowledge Base\.__ Both the Web App and PPT Add\-in will access the same underlying data through the backend services\.
